stimulus.title: Community repair cafe
stimulus.text: A volunteer repair cafe opened in Westford Town Hall last autumn. Residents bring small household items such as lamps, kettles, and radios to weekend sessions, where volunteers help diagnose faults and attempt simple repairs. The service does not accept large appliances or charge a repair fee, although visitors may donate toward replacement parts. Organisers say the main aim is to teach practical skills and reduce unnecessary waste. They have not measured whether the project has lowered household spending. A survey found that many visitors returned for a second session, but it did not compare Westford with repair cafes in other towns. The organisers believe local councils can support similar projects by providing safe workspace and basic tools rather than employing professional repair staff.
